message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted limits are the law.
• On highways: 55–75 mph (often 70 mph on rural interstates).
• In cities: 25–45 mph (often 35 mph).
• School zones: 20 mph during school hours. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑Belt & Child Restraint** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Failure to buckle can result in a $50 fine. | TxDOT – Seat Belt Law | | **DUI / Driving Under Influence** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) ≥ 0.08 % is illegal.
• Penalties: fines, license suspension, possible jail time.
• Zero‑Tolerance for drivers under 21. | Texas Alcoholic Beverage Commission (TABC) – DUI Laws | | **Texting & Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed.
• Violations can lead to a $50 fine. | TxDOT – Mobile Phone Use | | **Headlights & Visibility** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise and during inclement weather.
• Fog lights only when visibility ≤ 200 ft. | TxDOT – Lighting Regulations | | **Right‑of‑Way & Intersection Rules** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights; proceed on green.
• Turn signals must be used at least 100 ft before turning. | TxDOT – Traffic Signal & Intersection Rules | | **Parking & Loading Zones** | • No parking within 20 ft of a stop sign or crosswalk.
• Loading zones: 30 sec max unless otherwise posted. | TxDOT – Parking Regulations | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus stops to pick up/drop off children.
• Must remain stopped until the bus resumes motion. | TxDOT – School Bus Laws | | **Lane Discipline** | • Keep to the right lane unless passing.
• Do not drive in the left lane on freeways unless overtaking. | TxDOT – Lane Discipline | | **Vehicle Safety Standards** | • Vehicles must have functioning brakes, lights, turn signals, and seat belts.
• Regular inspections required for commercial vehicles. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) – Vehicle Inspection | | **Insurance Requirements** | • Minimum liability coverage: $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 for bodily injury per accident, $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Department of Insurance – Auto Insurance | --- ### How to Stay Updated 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The official legal text governing all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TX/htm/TX.HTM 2. **TxDOT Traffic Safety Division** – Offers educational materials, statistics, and updates on new regulations. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html 3. **Texas DMV** – Provides driver’s license information, vehicle registration, and inspection requirements. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/ 4. **Texas TABC** – For DUI laws, penalties, and sobriety checkpoints. *Website:* https://www.tabc.state.tx.us/ 5. **Local County Courts** – For specific local ordinances (e.g., city speed limits, parking restrictions). --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always obey posted speed limits** – they’re set for safety and road conditions. - **Use hands‑free devices** if you need to talk or navigate. - **Keep your vehicle well‑maintained** – brake pads, tires, lights, and mirrors. - **Plan ahead for school zones** – reduce speed and stay alert for children. - **Check for local ordinances** – some cities have stricter rules than state law. --- #### Need More Specific Information? If you’re looking for details on a particular aspect (e.g., commercial truck regulations, toll roads, or recent changes to Texas traffic law), let me know and I can dive deeper or point you to the exact statutes or resources.
